column3: The C flow controller was introduced mid-round, so initial work credit imports the already elapsed design and implementation interval; subsequent gate time remains measured automatically.

Task-run policy is class-dependent: review, analysis, docs, and verification default to none; development, environment, and cleanup default to compact result records; longrun and release use durable transaction evidence.

Postmortem retention stores structured engineering hypotheses, evidence, decisions, counterexamples, rollback points, and notes; it excludes private token-by-token reasoning, full chat transcripts, and duplicated raw payloads.
Final review consumes an explicit modified-path log instead of enumerating Git state, so concurrent user development cannot make the workflow snapshot stale or create avoidable worktree contention.

The roughly 40 percent workflow share is an advisory design and postmortem target, not a precise runtime gate. Gate duration remains observable, but exceeding the target never blocks delivery; task classification, caching, fixed pointers, and finish-only frequency reduce overhead.
Independent review runs once after the candidate delivery and validation summary exist. Read-only review tasks do not trigger recursive reviewer or guard layers.

A blanket flow-self-test on every environment finish recursively invoked the self-test when the advisory-overhead case executed a real gate, consuming about one minute. The selector now maps flow-self-test only from controller-related paths; the quick suite returns in about two seconds.

Pre-delivery review found that review and analysis could inject an explicit gate pointer despite their zero-gate contract. Record now rejects those pointers and gate derivation defensively returns an empty set; tests cover both classes.

Known GAP: an explicit modified-path log cannot automatically detect an unrecorded workspace write. This remains a caller/reviewer contract; Git worktree enumeration is intentionally not reintroduced because it conflicts with concurrent user development.
